html:
The Battle of Dyrrhachium was fought on 18 October 1081 outside Dyrrhachium, modern Durrës in Albania, the main Byzantine stronghold on the Adriatic. The Normans of southern Italy under Robert Guiscard defeated the new emperor Alexios I Komnenos.

The Normans had already taken Byzantine southern Italy and Arab Sicily. In 1081 Robert crossed the Adriatic with his son Bohemond to conquer the empire itself and laid siege to Dyrrhachium. Alexios brought an army to relieve it. His Varangian Guard, by now largely English exiles who hated the Normans after 1066, charged ahead of the rest and was cut off and destroyed. The Norman knights then broke the Byzantine line, and Alexios barely escaped.

Dyrrhachium fell early in 1082. Alexios turned to Venice, whose fleet fought the Normans at sea, and paid with the Golden Bull of trade privileges. The Norman threat lasted until Robert died in 1085. Anna Komnene describes the battle in her history of her father.
